task: Fix mobile (<=900px) rail layout: stop the horizontal-scroll rail bug and the #root height-pinning bug found by a mobile design critique (docs/design-critique/03-mobile-navigability-2026-07-24.md)

public/styles/responsive.css.summary: The <=900px query no longer flips .operatorRail/.railBody to flex-direction:row+overflow-x:auto (that collapsed the whole sidebar into a sideways-scrolling strip). .operatorRail now stays a vertical column (height:auto; overflow:visible). Also overrides html/body/#root height (not just overflow) at this breakpoint, since #root is the same node as .meetingShell and its ID selector in base.css otherwise outranks any class-selector override on specificity, silently pinning the page to 100dvh.

test/public/style.test.js.summary: Updated 'layout stacks and scrolls on narrower screens' to assert the corrected mobile rail behavior (vertical column, no flex-direction:row) instead of the old buggy expectation; added an assertion that html/body/#root override height, not just overflow.

flow_impact: none — no flow paths cross the mobile CSS breakpoint layer
